title: Subbing for Big Eye Louie Nelson at Lake Pontchartrain picnics
summary: Subbing at lake picnics for Big Eye Louie Nelson, Bigard was teased by Zutty Singleton as a snake charmer, held one wrong note, and was comforted by banjoist Willie Bontemps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: How old were you when you bought your B-flat clarinet?

Oh, about 14 years old.
Now, this I have to tell you. You know, I had a friend, a good friend of mine, Big Eye Louie Nelson. He was a clarinet player. Usually people at clubs used to give picnics on Sundays out at Lake Pontchartrain and they'd hired him. And sometimes he'd be so tired he couldn't make it, so he'd get off and stop by the house and ask me to go and play in his place. So Zutty Singleton was in the band with Sidney Desvignes and all of them. And at the lake, you know, sometime the hall would be way out in the lake and you could walk up. They had a little walk path -- a little walk to get there, and when the wind would be blowing in, you could hear them talking, you know. It's like an echo.
So I was getting off the train and walking out there and Zutty spied me, you know. He said, "My God, look who that character sent out here today. That snake charmer." And, boy, and he says, "Oh, we're going to suffer today." So I didn't care, you know. I had a hard face because I was learning all the time, you know. And Zutty's uncle, a fellow played the banjo called Willie Bontemps -- and he's a very nice man -- and I had to sit next to him. So he says, "Son, don't pay them no mind." He says, "Do your best." He

says, 'Don't worry.' So we started playing some number and I was trying to jazz it up and I couldn't make them notes and the chord and I hit one note and I just held that note all the way, and Zutty said, 'Get off that damn note, get off. Cut that note off.' And I just held that note and I stopped that note so short. He hollered at me and I started almost to crying, and Willie put his arms around me. He said, 'Don't worry, son, I'll take care of you.' And every time I'd see Zutty we'd start laughing about that. I'd say, 'I'm going to hold that note on you when I catch you.'

He called me a snake charmer. Oh, we used to -- I had a lot of fun, though. But that's the only way I learned. I mean, I didn't care -- I mean, I played parades. Nine o'clock in the morning and playing in a parade till five in the evening.
